hints: Notice the two nodes joined by the $2.0\text{ V}$ cell and galvanometer: one is left of $R$ and the other is between the $2.0\,\Omega$ and $10\,\Omega$ resistors.
Recall that zero galvanometer current means the $2.0\text{ V}$ cell exactly balances the potential divider p.d. between those two nodes, so $V_{R+2.0} = 2.0\text{ V}$.
Use the divider ratio with the $6.0\text{ V}$ supply across $R+2.0+10$ in $\Omega$ to set $6.0 \times (R+2.0)/(R+12) = 2.0$ and solve for $R$.
walkthrough: Identify the balanced section: the lower $2.0\text{ V}$ cell connects across the series combination of $R$ and the $2.0\,\Omega$ resistor.
State the null condition: when galvanometer current is zero there is no p.d. across the galvanometer branch, so the divider p.d. across $R+2.0\,\Omega$ must equal $2.0\text{ V}$.
Write the potential divider equation for the $6.0\text{ V}$ supply driving current through total resistance $R+2.0+10$ in $\Omega$: $V = 6.0 \times (R+2.0)/(R+2.0+10)$.
Set this equal to the balance voltage: $6.0(R+2.0)/(R+12) = 2.0$.
Solve: divide by $2.0$ to get $3(R+2.0) = R+12$, so $3R+6.0 = R+12$ and $2R = 6.0$, giving $R = 3.0\,\Omega$.

options.A: At balance the $2.0\text{ V}$ equals the divider p.d. across $R+2.0\,\Omega$, giving $R = 3.0\,\Omega$.
options.B: This value does not make the p.d. across $R+2.0\,\Omega$ equal to $2.0\text{ V}$ when divided from $6.0\text{ V}$.
options.C: This would make the p.d. across $R+2.0\,\Omega$ larger than $2.0\text{ V}$ because $R+2.0\,\Omega$ would be half the total resistance.
options.D: This confuses the balance length with the $10\,\Omega$ side and gives far too large a p.d. across $R+2.0\,\Omega$.
